The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=6$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=3.$

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=3$ and $x=9.$*

${f}^{′}(6)≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h},
$$

at the point $x=6$ with step size $h=3.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(6) & ≈\frac{f(6+3)-f(6-3)}{2(3)} \\  & =\frac{f(9)-f(3)}{6} \\  & =\frac{3-6}{6} \\  & =\frac{(-3)}{6} \\  & =-0.5.\end{aligned}
$$
